questions.question: What is the average of all the natural numbers from 1 to 60?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Consecutive numbers ⇒ average = (first + last) ÷ 2

⇒ = (1 + 60) ÷ 2 = 61 ÷ 2

⇒ = 30.5

**∴ Answer = 30.5**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Natural numbers from 1 to 60

**Formula:**

Average = (Sum of numbers) ÷ Total numbers

Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n + 1) ÷ 2

**Calculation:**

⇒ Sum = 60 × 61 ÷ 2 = 1830

⇒ Total numbers = 60

⇒ Average = 1830 ÷ 60 = 30.5

**∴ Final Answer = 30.5**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Consecutive Numbers:** Average = (First + Last) ÷ 2

**Sum Formula:** n(n+1) ÷ 2

**Key Insight:** Middle value represents average

**Tip:** Use shortcut instead of full summation

questions.question: Who deciphered a Brahmi inscription referring king Ashoka as Devanampiya Piyadasi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James Princep**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Princep** was an **English scholar**, **orientalist**, and an officer in the **Calcutta Mint** of the **East India Company**.
 
• In the year **1837**, he successfully deciphered the **Brahmi** and **Kharosthi** scripts, which were used in the earliest inscriptions and coins of ancient India.
 
• Through his research, he identified that the inscriptions referring to a king named **Devanampiya Piyadasi** (meaning **"Beloved of the Gods"** and **"of Pleasant Gaze"**) were actually referring to the **Mauryan Emperor Ashoka**.
 
• This breakthrough allowed historians to correlate archaeological evidence with **Buddhist chronicles** like the **Dipavamsa** and **Mahavamsa**, establishing **Ashoka** as one of the greatest rulers in **Indian history**. ***Hence, the statement regarding James Princep is correct.***
 
• The identification of these inscriptions provided a **chronological framework** for **ancient Indian history**, which was previously based largely on legends and myths.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **R C Majumdar:**

 
 
• **Ramesh Chandra Majumdar** (**1888–1980**) was a prominent **Indian historian** known for his monumental work **"The History and Culture of the Indian People"**.
 
• While he contributed extensively to the study of **ancient India** and **Bengal**, he was not the one who deciphered the **Brahmi script**.
 
 
 
• **Romila Thapar:**
 
 
• **Romila Thapar** is a world-renowned **Indian historian** whose primary focus is **Ancient India**.
 
• She is well-known for her book **"Ashoka and the Decline of the Mauryas"**, published in **1961**, which offers a **socio-economic analysis** of the **Mauryan Empire**.
 
• Her work interprets the **Dhamma of Ashoka** as a **civic code** rather than a religious doctrine.
 
 
 
• **Susan Bayly:**
 
 
• **Susan Bayly** is a professor of **Historical Anthropology** at the **University of Cambridge**.
 
• Her research focuses on **caste**, **society**, and **colonialism** in **South Asia** and **Southeast Asia**, particularly **Vietnam**.
 
• She is the author of **"Caste, Society and Politics in India from the Eighteenth Century to the Modern Age"**.
 
 
 
• **Brahmi Script:**
 
 
• It is the **ancestor** of almost all modern **Indian scripts** and was used by **Ashoka** for his **Rock Edicts** and **Pillar Edicts**.
 
• The script was primarily written from **left to right**, and its decipherment opened the door to understanding **Magadhi Prakrit**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Epigraphy:** The study of **inscriptions** is known as **epigraphy**. The decipherment by **James Princep** is considered the most significant milestone in **Indian epigraphy**.
 
• **Maski Inscription:** Although **James Princep** linked **Piyadasi** to **Ashoka**, the final confirmation came in **1915** when an inscription was found at **Maski** in **Karnataka** that explicitly mentioned the name **"Ashoka"** alongside **"Devanampiya"**.
 
• **Asiatic Society:** **James Princep** served as the **founding editor** of the **Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal**, which published his findings on **Ashokan pillars** located in **Delhi** and **Allahabad**.
 
• **Kharosthi Script:** Unlike **Brahmi**, **Kharosthi** was written from **right to left** and was used primarily in the **Northwest** regions of the **Indian subcontinent**, such as **Gandhara** (modern-day **Pakistan** and **Afghanistan**).

questions.question: Which of the following is correct with respect to the theme of Yamuna Paryatam, the first novel in Marathi?

options.text: Focused on Political life of Yamuna region

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Criticized Hindu practices regarding widows**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yamuna Paryatam**, published in **1857**, is widely regarded as the **first novel** in the **Marathi language**. It was written by **Baba Padmanji**, a prominent social reformer and convert to Christianity.
 
• The central theme of the novel is the **plight of widows** in contemporary **Hindu society**. It vividly describes the physical and mental suffering they endured, including the practice of **shaving heads (tonsure)** and social boycotts. ***Hence, the statement that it criticized Hindu practices regarding widows is correct.***
 
• The narrative follows the journey of a young woman named **Yamuna** and her husband **Vinayak** as they travel and witness the miserable conditions of widows across various places. This journey serves as a medium for social commentary.
 
• **Statement 1**: The novel did not focus on **adventure stories**. While it involves travel, the primary objective was **social reform** rather than escapism or thrill-seeking adventure. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2**: It did not focus on the **political life** of the **Yamuna region**. The title "Yamuna Paryatam" refers to the protagonist's name, **Yamuna**, and her "Paryatam" (travels), rather than the geography of the Yamuna River or political administration. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4**: The novel did not **praise Hindu customs**; instead, it was a sharp **critique** of orthodox **Brahminical traditions** that oppressed women and denied them the right to **remarry**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Baba Padmanji (1831-1906)**: He was a significant figure in the **19th-century** social reform movement in **Maharashtra**. He was born into a **Kasari** family but later embraced **Christianity** in **1854**. His writings often reflected the **interplay between Christian ethics** and the need for **Hindu social reform**.
 
• **Advocacy for Remarriage**: One of the core messages of **Yamuna Paryatam** was the promotion of **widow remarriage**. At the end of the novel, the protagonist **Yamuna**, after becoming a widow herself, chooses to **remarry** and convert to Christianity, symbolizing a break from oppressive traditional bonds.
 
• **Literary Significance**: Before this work, **Marathi literature** largely consisted of poetry and religious texts. **Yamuna Paryatam** introduced the **prose narrative form** to the masses, paving the way for the development of the **modern Marathi novel**.
 
• **Historical Context**: The novel was written during a period of intense **intellectual ferment** in **India**, specifically in **Bombay (Mumbai)** and **Poona (Pune)**, where reformers like **Jyotirao Phule** were also beginning to challenge **caste and gender hierarchies**.
 
• **Impact on Women's Rights**: By highlighting the **domestic violence** and **emotional trauma** faced by women, the book played a crucial role in bringing **women's issues** to the forefront of the **public discourse** in **Western India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Social Realism**: The book is considered an early example of **social realism** in Indian literature. It did not shy away from depicting the **harsh realities** of the **caste system** and **patriarchy**.
 
• **Language and Style**: **Baba Padmanji** used a **simple and direct** style of **Marathi**, making the book accessible to the common person rather than just the learned **Shastris** or **Pandits**.
 
• **Year of Publication**: **1857** is a landmark year in Indian history due to the **Great Revolt**, and the publication of this novel in the same year highlights that **social revolutions** were occurring alongside **political upheavals**.
 
• **Religious Influence**: The novel also acted as a piece of **Christian apologetics**, suggesting that the **liberation of women** could be found through the adoption of **Christian values**, which was a common theme among **19th-century converts**.

questions.question: Which of the following administrative features was a key characteristic of the Mauryan Empire under Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Centralised bureaucracy guided by Arthashastra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mauryan Empire**, founded by **Chandragupta Maurya** in approximately **322 BCE**, was characterized by a highly sophisticated and **centralised bureaucracy**. This system ensured that the central government had direct control over various aspects of the state, from revenue to security. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The administrative framework was heavily influenced by the **Arthashastra**, a classic treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy authored by **Chanakya** (also known as **Kautilya** or **Vishnugupta**), who was the Prime Minister and mentor to **Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• The empire was divided into provinces, usually headed by a **Kumara** (prince) or a member of the royal family. Unlike later medieval systems, these provincial governors were **appointed officials** and not **hereditary** rulers, ensuring the King's authority remained absolute. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The Mauryan economy was largely state-controlled, and land revenue was the primary source of income. The **feudal land grant system**, where land was given to intermediaries in exchange for military service, was a feature that developed much later during the **Gupta period** and the early medieval era. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Revenue collection was a strictly secular and administrative function carried out by state officials like the **Samaharta** (Chief Collector). **Religious institutions** did not have the authority to collect state taxes; instead, they were often recipients of state patronage. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the Central Government:**

 
 
• The **King** was the fountainhead of all authority, assisted by a council of ministers called the **Mantriparishad**.
 
• The bureaucracy was composed of a hierarchy of officials known as **Amatyas** (civil servants) and **Adhyakshas** (superintendents of various departments).
 
• There were nearly **27-30 departments** managing diverse sectors like **agriculture** (Sita-adhyaksha), **commerce** (Panyadhyaksha), and **weights and measures** (Pautavadhyaksha).
 
 
 
• **Municipal Administration:**
 
 
• The Greek ambassador **Megasthenes**, in his work **Indica**, provides a detailed account of the administration of the capital city, **Pataliputra**.
 
• The city was managed by **six committees** of **five members** each, looking after industries, foreigners, births and deaths, trade, manufactured goods, and the collection of the **tenth of the prices** as tax.
 
 
 
• **The Espionage System:**
 
 
• A unique feature of the Mauryan state was its extensive network of **spies**, referred to as **Gudha Purushas**.
 
• Spies were categorized into **Sanstha** (stationary) and **Sanchari** (wandering), reporting directly to the **King** about the loyalty of officials and the pulse of the public.
 
 
 
• **Military Strength:**
 
 
• The Mauryan army was massive, consisting of **infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants**. **Pliny** and **Megasthenes** mention that **Chandragupta Maurya** maintained an army of **6,00,000 infantry**, **30,000 cavalry**, and **9,000 elephants**.
 
• The military was administered by a board of **30 members** divided into **six committees** of **five members** each.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Saptanga Theory:** **Kautilya** described the state as having **seven limbs** (Saptanga): **Swami** (The King), **Amatya** (The Ministers), **Janapada** (The Territory/People), **Durga** (The Fortification), **Kosha** (The Treasury), **Danda** (The Army), and **Mitra** (The Ally).
 
• **Diplomatic Relations:** **Chandragupta Maurya** defeated the Greek general **Seleucus Nicator** in **305 BCE**, leading to a treaty where the Mauryan Empire gained territories like **Arachosia** (Kandahar) and **Gedrosia** (Baluchistan).
 
• **Public Welfare:** Despite being highly centralized, the state focused on **public works**, including the construction of the **Royal Road** (precursor to the Grand Trunk Road) and irrigation projects like the **Sudarshana Lake** in **Junagadh, Gujarat**.

questions.question: What is the maximum value that must be assigned to A so that the 8-digit number 445A0208 is divisible by 3?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Sum of digits = 4+4+5+A+0+2+0+8 = 23 + A

⇒ For divisibility by 3 ⇒ (23 + A) divisible by 3

⇒ 23 mod 3 = 2 ⇒ Need A mod 3 = 1

⇒ Possible A: 1, 4, 7 ⇒ max = 7

**∴ Answer = 7**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 445A0208

**Formula Used:**

A number is divisible by 3 if sum of digits is divisible by 3

**Calculation:**

⇒ Sum of known digits = 4 + 4 + 5 + 0 + 2 + 0 + 8 = 23

⇒ Total sum = 23 + A

⇒ Required: (23 + A) divisible by 3

⇒ Check largest A (0 to 9):

⇒ A = 9 ⇒ 32 (not divisible)

⇒ A = 8 ⇒ 31 (not divisible)

⇒ A = 7 ⇒ 30 (divisible)

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Divisibility Rule (3):** Sum of digits divisible by 3

**Digit Range:** A can be 0 to 9

**Modulo Trick:** Work with remainders

**Exam Tip:** Check largest valid digit

questions.question: In most web browsers, when multiple tabs are open in a web browser, pressing Ctrl + Tab performs which action?

options.text: Navigates to the previous tab on the left
Navigates to the next tab on the right

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Navigates to the next tab on the right**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In modern web browsers such as **Google Chrome**, **Mozilla Firefox**, **Microsoft Edge**, and **Safari**, the shortcut **Ctrl + Tab** is used for tab navigation.
 
• When a user has multiple tabs open, pressing **Ctrl + Tab** moves the focus to the **next tab on the right** side of the current active tab. ***Hence, the statement regarding navigating to the next tab on the right is correct.***
 
• The action of **launching a new tab** is typically performed using the shortcut **Ctrl + T** in Windows/Linux. ***Hence, the statement regarding launching a new tab is incorrect.***
 
• The action of **removing or closing the selected tab** is performed using **Ctrl + W** or **Ctrl + F4**. ***Hence, the statement regarding removing the selected tab is incorrect.***
 
• To **navigate to the previous tab on the left**, the user must press **Ctrl + Shift + Tab**. ***Hence, the statement regarding navigating to the previous tab on the left is incorrect.***
 
• This shortcut allows for efficient **multitasking** without the need for a **mouse** or **trackpad**, significantly increasing **productivity** for power users.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Browser Tab Management:**

 
 
• **Ctrl + Shift + T**: This is an essential command used to **reopen the last closed tab**. It is extremely useful if a tab was closed by **accident**.
 
• **Ctrl + 1 through 8**: Pressing **Ctrl** along with a **numerical value** from **1 to 8** will switch the focus to that specific **tab number** (counting from the left).
 
• **Ctrl + 9**: This shortcut immediately switches to the **last tab** opened in the window, regardless of how many tabs are active.
 
 
 
• **Window and Navigation Shortcuts:**
 
 
• **Ctrl + N**: Opens a **new browser window**.
 
• **Ctrl + Shift + N**: In **Google Chrome**, this opens a new **Incognito window** for private browsing. In **Firefox**, the equivalent is **Ctrl + Shift + P** for a **Private Window**.
 
• **Ctrl + L** or **Alt + D**: Moves the cursor focus directly to the **Address Bar** (Omnibox), allowing the user to type a new **URL** or search query immediately.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Tabbed browsing was popularized in the **early 2000s** by browsers like **Opera** and **Firefox**, moving away from the single-window model of early **Internet Explorer** versions. The **Ctrl + Tab** convention was adopted to mirror the **Alt + Tab** function used by **Windows** to switch between **applications**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Operating System Differences:**

 
 
• On **macOS**, the **Command (⌘)** key is used instead of the **Control (Ctrl)** key for most functions. For example, **Command + Option + Right Arrow** or **Control + Tab** can be used to switch tabs in **Safari** on **Mac**.
 
• In some browsers like **Firefox**, the behavior of **Ctrl + Tab** can be customized in the **settings** to cycle through tabs in **recently used order** rather than purely sequential **left-to-right** order.
 
 
 
• **Efficiency and Accessibility:**
 
 
• Keyboard shortcuts are a vital part of **web accessibility** guidelines, ensuring that users with **motor impairments** who cannot use a mouse can still navigate the web effectively using a **keyboard**.
 
• In **2024**, most browsers also support **Vertical Tabs** (notably **Microsoft Edge**), but the **Ctrl + Tab** shortcut remains the universal standard for cycling through the list.

questions.question: At what rate (in percentage, rounded off to two decimal place) per year will a sum of money 5 times itself in 12 years on simple interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Final = 5P ⇒ Interest = 4P

⇒ SI = P × r × t / 100 ⇒ 4P = P × r × 12 / 100

⇒ r = (4 × 100) / 12 = 33.33%

**∴ Answer = 33.33%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount becomes 5 times in 12 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × r × t) / 100

Amount = P + SI

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let principal = P

⇒ Amount = 5P

⇒ SI = 5P − P = 4P

⇒ Using SI formula:

⇒ 4P = (P × r × 12) / 100

⇒ Cancel P:

⇒ 4 = (r × 12) / 100

⇒ r = (4 × 100) / 12

⇒ r = 33.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Simple Interest:** SI = (P × r × t)/100

**Amount Relation:** A = P + SI

**Shortcut:** Multiply factor − 1 gives interest multiple

**Exam Tip:** Cancel P early

questions.question: The minimum value of the expression max {p² − 2p + 4, −p² + 2p − 4} in the range 0 ≤ p ≤ 1 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check endpoints (max function minimum occurs at edges)

p = 0 ⇒ max{4, −4} = 4

p = 1 ⇒ max{3, −3} = 3

⇒ Minimum = 3

**∴ Answer = 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = max {p² − 2p + 4, −p² + 2p − 4}

Range: 0 ≤ p ≤ 1

**Formula:**

For minimum of max, compare both expressions

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let f = p² − 2p + 4

⇒ g = −p² + 2p − 4

⇒ Note: g = −f

⇒ So expression = max(f, −f) = |f|

⇒ f = (p − 1)² + 3 ≥ 3

⇒ Minimum at p = 1

⇒ Value = 3

**∴ Final Answer = 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Max Function:** max(a, b) picks larger value

**Symmetry:** max(f, −f) = |f|

**Quadratic Min:** (x − a)² ≥ 0

**Tip:** Convert to modulus for speed

__
 
• **Puducherry** is one of the few **Union Territories** in India that possesses its own **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers** headed by a **Chief Minister**.
 
• The **14th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962**, led to the creation of **Puducherry** as a **Union Territory** and provided for the establishment of a legislature and council of ministers.

• **Delhi (National Capital Territory)**: It was provided with a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers** through the **69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991**, which inserted **Article 239AA** into the **Constitution**.

• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**: Established as a **Union Territory** in **1956**, it is located in the **Bay of Bengal** and is administered by a **Lieutenant Governor** without a local legislature.

• Unlike **States**, the **Union Territories** are considered **federal units** that are under the direct control and supervision of the **Union Government** of **India**.

__
 
• In the **year 2025**, **India** reached a significant landmark in its journey toward global sustainability by entering the **top 100** countries in the **UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** rankings for the first time. This reflects a consistent improvement from its **109th** position recorded in **2024**.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report**, published annually by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**, evaluates the progress of **193 UN Member States** in achieving the **17 SDGs**.
 
• The milestone was achieved due to **India's** proactive implementation of large-scale social welfare schemes that align with the **2030 Agenda**. The improvement in the index score indicates that **India** has made substantial strides in reconciling economic growth with environmental and social objectives.
 
• Key sectors contributing to this rise include **SDG 1 (No Poverty)**, **SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation)**, and **SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities)**. The targeted delivery of services through digital public infrastructure has been a major catalyst in this achievement.
 
• While **India achieved all SDGs** is an incorrect statement as the target year is **2030** and no country has fully achieved them yet, **India's** entry into the **top 100** marks a shift from being a "performer" to a "front runner" in various global categories.

• **The 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**

It categorizes them into four groups based on their composite score: **Aspirant (0–49)**, **Performer (50–64)**, **Front Runner (65–99)**, and **Achiever (100)**.
 
 
 
• **Global Rankings and SDSN:**
 
 
• The **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** has been operating since **2012** under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General**. The global ranking is influenced by the **SDG Index Score**, where **Finland**, **Sweden**, and **Denmark** have traditionally held the top spots.
 
 
 
• **India's Major Interventions:**
 
 
• Schemes such as the **Jal Jeevan Mission** (aiming for **100%** tap water connectivity), **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana** (housing for all), and the **Ayushman Bharat** (world's largest health insurance scheme) have been instrumental in improving **India's** global standing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** In **2023** and **2024**, **India** hovered around the **112th** to **109th** rank. The jump to the **top 100** in **2025** signifies an accelerated pace of development and better data reporting mechanisms on international platforms.
 
• **Challenges in Specific Goals:** Despite the overall rank improvement, **India** still faces challenges in **SDG 2 (Zero Hunger)** and **SDG 5 (Gender Equality)**. Addressing **stunting and wasting** among children remains a priority for the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**.
 
• **SDG 13 (Climate Action):** **India** is one of the few **G20** nations on track to meet its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the **Paris Agreement**, which significantly boosts its **SDG Index** performance compared to many developed countries.

questions.question: Which of the following theories was propounded in Dadabhai Naoroji’s 1901 book Poverty and Un-British Rule in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Drain of Wealth Theory**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**, popularly known as the **"Grand Old Man of India"**, propounded the **Drain of Wealth Theory** in his seminal book **"Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"** published in **1901**.
 
• The theory highlights the constant flow of **wealth** from **India** to **England**, for which India received no adequate economic or material return. This systematic **drain** was identified as the primary cause of **poverty** in India during the **British colonial period**.
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was the first **Indian** to attempt the estimation of **National Income**. In **1867-68**, he calculated the per capita income of Indians to be **Rs. 20** per year, showcasing the extreme economic hardship under **British** administration.
 
• The **Drain of Wealth** was manifested through various channels such as **Home Charges** (expenditure incurred in England by the Secretary of State on behalf of India), interest on **foreign debt**, and salaries/pensions of **British** officials.
 
• His work provided a scientific and statistical foundation for **economic nationalism** in India, challenging the **British** claim that their rule was beneficial for the Indian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Subsidiary Alliance Theory**:

 
 
• This was a **non-intervention** policy used by **Lord Wellesley**, the **Governor-General** of India from **1798** to **1805**.
 
• Under this system, the ruler of an allying **Indian State** was compelled to accept the permanent stationing of a **British** force within his territory and pay a **subsidy** for its maintenance.
 
• The **Nizam of Hyderabad** was the first to enter into a **Subsidiary Alliance** with the **British** in **1798**.
 
 
 
• **Doctrine of Lapse Theory**:
 
 
• This was an **annexation** policy followed by **Lord Dalhousie**, who served as the **Governor-General** from **1848** to **1856**.
 
• According to this doctrine, any **Princely State** under the direct or indirect influence of the **British** would be annexed if the ruler died without a **natural heir** (adopted heirs were not recognized for the purpose of succession to the throne).
 
• **Satara** (**1848**), **Sambalpur** (**1849**), **Jhansi** (**1853**), and **Nagpur** (**1854**) were prominent states annexed under this policy.
 
 
 
• **Two Nation Theory**:
 
 
• This theory proposed that **Hindus** and **Muslims** were two distinct nations with different **cultures**, **religions**, and **customs**, and therefore could not live together in one country.
 
• While its roots are often traced back to **Sir Syed Ahmed Khan**, it was later championed by **Muhammad Ali Jinnah** and the **Muslim League**, leading to the **Partition of India** in **1947**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was the first **Indian** to be elected as a **Member of Parliament (MP)** in the **British House of Commons**, representing the **Finsbury Central** constituency from **1892** to **1895**.
 
• He played a crucial role in the formation of the **Indian National Congress (INC)** and served as its **President** three times: in **1886** (Calcutta), **1893** (Lahore), and **1906** (Calcutta).
 
• During the **1906** session of the **INC**, he was the leader who first used the word **"Swaraj"** (Self-rule) from the Congress platform as the ultimate goal for the Indian people.
 
• He founded the **London Indian Society** in **1865** and the **East India Association** in **1866** to put forward **Indian** viewpoints across to the **British** public and **Parliament**.

questions.question: Which natural disaster involves mass movement of snow, ice, and rock down a mountain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Avalanche**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **Avalanche** is a natural disaster characterized by the rapid **mass movement** of **snow**, **ice**, **soil**, and **rock** down a **mountain slope**. It occurs when the **shear stress** on the snowpack exceeds its **shear strength**.
 
• These events are most common in **high-altitude** mountainous regions such as the **Himalayas** in **India**, the **Alps** in **Europe**, and the **Rockies** in **North America**.
 
• The primary triggers for an **Avalanche** include **heavy snowfall**, **wind-loading**, **rapid temperature rise**, and **seismic activity** like **earthquakes**. **Human activities**, such as **skiing**, **snowmobiling**, or **construction** in hilly areas, can also trigger these slides.
 
• An **Avalanche** can reach speeds of up to **200 kilometers per hour** (approx. **124 miles per hour**), making it one of the most dangerous **geophysical hazards** for **climbers**, **skiers**, and **mountain residents**.
 
• The **Avalanche** involving snow and ice is distinct from other mass movements because it specifically relies on the **thermal and structural properties** of the **snowpack** layers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Avalanches:**

 
 
• **Slab Avalanche**: This is the most dangerous type, where a **cohesive layer** of snow breaks off and slides down. It is often triggered by a **mechanical failure** in a **weak layer** of the snowpack.
 
• **Powder Snow Avalanche**: These consist of a **low-density** cloud of **suspended snow** that behaves like a fluid, often moving at **extreme velocities**.
 
• **Wet Snow Avalanche**: These occur due to **melting** during the **spring season** or after **rain-on-snow** events, moving more slowly but with **immense force**.
 
 
 
• **Prevention and Mitigation:**
 
 
• In countries like **Switzerland** and **Canada**, **snow fences** and **deflection dams** are built to protect **highways** and **railways**.
 
• **Controlled explosions** are used by **mountain safety teams** to trigger small, harmless slides before the **snow accumulation** becomes critical.
 
• **Afforestation** (planting trees) on slopes acts as a **natural barrier** against small to medium-sized **Avalanches**.
 
 
 
• **Impact and Data:**
 
 
• Every **year**, hundreds of lives are lost globally due to **Avalanches**. In **2012**, the **Gayari Sector avalanche** in **Siachen** resulted in the death of over **130 soldiers**.
 
• The **snow-ice** mix in an avalanche can become as hard as **concrete** once it stops moving, making **rescue operations** extremely difficult.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cyclone**: This is a **meteorological phenomenon** characterized by **low atmospheric pressure** and **strong winds** rotating inward. It typically forms over **warm ocean waters**. *Hence, this option is incorrect as it does not involve the downward movement of snow on mountains.*
 
• **Tsunami**: This refers to a series of **giant ocean waves** caused by **underwater disturbances** such as **tectonic shifts** or **submarine volcanic eruptions**. It affects **coastal regions**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Landslide**: A **Landslide** is a broad term for the **downward movement** of **rock**, **debris**, or **earth**. While similar to an avalanche, a landslide typically refers to **soil-based** movement, whereas the question specifically highlights **snow and ice**. *Hence, while related to mass movement, it is not the most specific answer for snow.*
 
• **Geographic Distribution**: In **India**, the **Snow and Avalanche Study Establishment (SASE)**, a laboratory of **DRDO**, is responsible for monitoring and **forecasting avalanches** in the **Himalayan region**.

questions.question: Which global event in 1992 popularized sustainable development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rio Earth Summit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rio Earth Summit**, officially known as the **United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED)**, was held in **Rio de Janeiro, Brazil**, from **3 to 14 June 1992**. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• This global event was a major milestone that popularized the concept of **Sustainable Development**, defined as development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
 
• The summit resulted in several landmark documents, including **Agenda 21** (a blueprint for sustainable development in the 21st century), the **Rio Declaration on Environment and Development**, and the **Statement of Forest Principles**.
 
• It also led to the creation of vital international treaties, namely the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)** and the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)**.
 
• The conference saw participation from **172 governments**, with **108 attendance at the level of heads of state or government**, making it one of the largest gatherings of world leaders at the time to address environmental issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Montreal Protocol (1987):**

 
 
• The **Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer** is an international treaty designed to protect the **ozone layer**.
 
• It was signed on **16 September 1987** and focuses on phasing out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances like **chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** and **halons**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Kyoto Protocol (1997):**
 
 
• The **Kyoto Protocol** was adopted in **Kyoto, Japan**, on **11 December 1997** and entered into force in **2005**.
 
• It was an extension of the **1992 UNFCCC** that committed industrialized countries and economies in transition to limit and reduce **greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions** in accordance with agreed individual targets. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement (2015):**
 
 
• The **Paris Agreement** is a legally binding international treaty on **climate change** adopted by **196 parties** at **COP 21** in **Paris** on **12 December 2015**.
 
• Its primary goal is to limit global warming to well below **2 degrees Celsius**, preferably to **1.5 degrees Celsius**, compared to pre-industrial levels. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Definition of Sustainable Development:**
 
 
• While the **Rio Summit** popularized the term, the formal definition was first introduced in the **Brundtland Report** (also titled **Our Common Future**) published in **1987** by the **World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Agenda 21:** This is a **comprehensive plan of action** to be taken globally, nationally, and locally by organizations of the **United Nations System**, Governments, and Major Groups in every area in which human impacts on the environment.
 
• **UNFCCC:** Established during the **1992 summit**, it serves as the parent treaty of the **2015 Paris Agreement** and the **1997 Kyoto Protocol**.
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** Building on the momentum of the **Rio Summit** and subsequent meetings like **Rio+20 (2012)**, the UN adopted the **17 Sustainable Development Goals** in **2015** to be achieved by the year **2030**.

questions.question: Which of the following online festivals featured documentaries on Indian classical dance exponents in 2020?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The online festival titled **Nrityanjali** was organized by the **Films Division**, under the **Ministry of Information and Broadcasting**, **Government of India**.
 
• The festival was held from **September 23 to September 25, 2020**, as a digital initiative to bring the heritage of **Indian classical dance** to the public during the **COVID-19** pandemic.
 
• The primary objective of **Nrityanjali** was to showcase documentaries that chronicled the lives, struggles, and artistic excellence of legendary dance exponents who have shaped India’s cultural landscape.
 
• The festival featured biographical films on icons such as **Rukmini Devi Arundale** (Bharatanatyam), **Pandit Birju Maharaj** (Kathak), **Kelucharan Mohapatra** (Odissi), and **Yamini Krishnamurthy** (Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi).

__
 
• **Indian Classical Dances:**

 
 
• There are currently **8 classical dances** recognized by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**: **Bharatanatyam** (Tamil Nadu), **Kathak** (North India), **Kathakali** (Kerala), **Kuchipudi** (Andhra Pradesh), **Odissi** (Odisha), **Manipuri** (Manipur), **Mohiniyattam** (Kerala), and **Sattriya** (Assam).

• **Exponents Mentioned in the Festival:**

• **Pandit Birju Maharaj**: A doyen of the **Lucknow Kalka-Bindadin Gharana** of **Kathak**, he was a recipient of the **Padma Vibhushan** in **1986**.
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra**: He is credited with the revival of **Odissi** in the **20th century** and was the first person from **Odisha** to receive the **Padma Vibhushan** in **2000**.
 
 
 
• **Films Division of India:**
 
 
• Established in **1948**, it is headquartered in **Mumbai**.
 
• It serves as the main government agency to produce and distribute documentaries and news magazines for public education and the preservation of Indian history.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Natya Utsav**: This is a general term for drama or theater festivals. Many organizations like **Sahitya Kala Parishad** organize annual **Natya Utsavs** to promote stage plays.
 
• **Nritya Mahotsav**: This translates to "Dance Festival." Notable examples include the **Khajuraho Dance Festival** in **Madhya Pradesh** or the **Konark Festival** in **Odisha**, which are held annually to celebrate classical dance against the backdrop of heritage monuments.
 
• **Rangmanch**: This term literally means "**Stage**" or "**Theater**" in Hindi. It refers to the performing arts sector rather than a specific online documentary festival of **2020**.
 
• **Context of 2020**: During the **lockdown**, several cultural bodies shifted to the **OTT (Over-the-top)** or **virtual platform**. **Nrityanjali** was unique because it used archival **documentary films** rather than live-streamed performances to educate the youth about the history of classical arts.

questions.question: Which measurement method includes all those who are found unemployed in the reference year and reflects chronic unemployment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Usual Principal Status Unemployment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Usual Principal Status (UPS)** measurement is used to identify individuals who remained unemployed for a relatively longer period during the **365 days** preceding the date of the survey.
 
• Under this method, a person is classified as unemployed if he or she was available for work but did not find **gainful employment** for the **major part of the year** (i.e., **183 days** or more).
 
• This measurement specifically reflects **chronic unemployment** or **open unemployment**, as it focuses on the long-term status of an individual rather than temporary or seasonal fluctuations in the labor market.
 
• In **India**, the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)**, under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, traditionally uses this method to provide a comprehensive picture of the structural unemployment prevailing in the economy.
 
• This status is determined by the **major time criterion**, where the activity status (employed, unemployed, or out of the labor force) on which a person spent the maximum time during the **reference year** is recorded. Hence, the statement identifying UPS as the measure for chronic unemployment is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Usual Subsidiary Status (USS):**

 
 
• This refers to individuals who are classified as unemployed based on their **principal status** but might have worked for a short period of at least **30 days** during the **reference year**.
 
• When **Usual Principal Status** and **Subsidiary Status** are combined, it is known as **UPSS (Usual Principal and Subsidiary Status)**, which provides a broader estimate of the workforce by including part-time or intermittent workers.
 
 
 
• **Current Weekly Status (CWS):**
 
 
• The reference period for this measurement is the **seven days** preceding the date of the survey.
 
• A person is considered employed if they worked for at least **one hour** on any **one day** during the reference week.
 
• It is useful for capturing **seasonal unemployment** and short-term changes in the employment patterns of **India**.
 
 
 
• **Current Daily Status (CDS):**
 
 
• This is considered the most **rigorous** and accurate measure of unemployment and **underemployment**.
 
• It records the activity status of a person for each of the **seven days** in the reference week, measuring **person-days** rather than just individuals.
 
• It helps in understanding the **intensity of work** and is often used to calculate the **unemployment rate** in the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** reports.
 
 
 
• **Structural and Frictional Unemployment:**
 
 
• **Structural unemployment** occurs due to a mismatch between the skills of the **workforce** and the requirements of the **employers**, often found in developing nations like **India**.
 
• **Frictional unemployment** is temporary and occurs when individuals are **between jobs** or looking for better opportunities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statistical Background:** The concept of measuring unemployment through different statuses was recommended by the **Dantwala Committee** in **1970** to better understand the multi-dimensional nature of the **Indian labor market**.
 
• **PLFS Reports:** The **Periodic Labour Force Survey**, launched in **April 2017**, publishes annual reports that use **Usual Status** and **Current Weekly Status** to estimate the **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)** and **Worker Population Ratio (WPR)**.
 
• **Demographic Focus:** These measurements are crucial for drafting **government policies** like the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, which aims to provide **100 days** of wage employment to rural households to combat **chronic unemployment**.
 
• **Age Criteria:** In most surveys, the labor force is measured for the age group of **15 to 59 years**, which constitutes the **working-age population**.

questions.question: A rise in the sea surface temperature in the Pacific Ocean accompanied by deficient rainfall in India is associated with which of the following phenomena?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**El Nino**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **El Nino** is a climate pattern that describes the unusual warming of **surface waters** in the **central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean**. This phenomenon is the warm phase of a larger cycle called the **El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO)**.
 
• When **El Nino** occurs, the **Trade Winds** that normally blow from east to west along the **Equator** weaken or even reverse direction. This allows warm water to move toward the **coast of South America**, specifically near **Peru** and **Ecuador**.
 
• The rise in **Sea Surface Temperature (SST)** in the **Pacific Ocean** disrupts the global atmospheric circulation. In the context of **India**, this disruption often results in a weakening of the **Southwest Monsoon**.
 
• Deficient rainfall and **drought conditions** in **India** are frequently associated with **El Nino** years. Statistical data suggests that since **1950**, about **60%** of **El Nino** events have led to **droughts** in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The phenomenon typically occurs at irregular intervals of **2 to 7 years** and usually lasts for **nine to twelve months**, though it can sometimes persist for years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **La Nina:**

 
 
• Known as the **"cold phase"** of **ENSO**, it is the opposite of **El Nino**. It involves the **cooling** of surface waters in the **central and eastern Pacific**.
 
• In **India**, **La Nina** is generally associated with **above-normal rainfall** and a strong **Southwest Monsoon**, which is beneficial for **Kharif crops**.
 
 
 
• **ENSO Cycle:**
 
 
• The **El Nino-Southern Oscillation** consists of three phases: **El Nino** (warm), **La Nina** (cold), and a **Neutral phase**.
 
• Scientists monitor this using the **Oceanic Nino Index (ONI)**, which tracks the **SST** in the **Nino 3.4 region** of the **Pacific Ocean**.
 
 
 
• **Southern Oscillation:**
 
 
• This refers to the **atmospheric component** of the phenomenon, characterized by changes in **air pressure** between **Tahiti** (central Pacific) and **Darwin, Australia** (western Pacific).
 
• A negative **Southern Oscillation Index (SOI)** usually accompanies **El Nino** events.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• **El Nino** has severe **economic implications** for **India** because its **agriculture sector** is heavily dependent on **monsoon rainfall**. Deficits can lead to **inflation** in food prices.
 
• In **South America**, it affects **fisheries** as the warm water stops the **upwelling** of nutrient-rich cold water, drastically reducing the **fish population**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Walker Circulation:** This is the **east-west atmospheric circulation** over the **Equatorial Pacific**. During **El Nino**, this circulation breaks down or reverses, causing **convection** (and rain) to shift from the **Western Pacific** (near **Australia/Indonesia**) to the **Central/Eastern Pacific**.
 
• **Historical Context:** Severe **El Nino** years like **1997-1998** and **2015-2016** were among the strongest on record, causing **global temperature spikes** and extreme weather events worldwide.
 
• **Nomenclature:** The name **El Nino** is **Spanish** for **"The Little Boy"** or **"Christ Child,"** coined by **Peruvian fishermen** because the warming often peaked around **December** (Christmas time).
 
• **Teleconnections:** This term describes how weather changes in the **Pacific** affect distant locations like **India**, **Africa**, and **North America**. For **India**, the **teleconnection** manifests as suppressed rainfall due to the shifting of **low-pressure zones**.

questions.question:
In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer.

Q. Kunal, Mohit, Rohan, Sandeep, and Tarun - each have different age. Who is the oldest?

(I) Mohit is older than Kunal but younger than Sandeep.

(II) Tarun is younger than Sandeep but older than Mohit.

options.text: Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement I is not
Both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement II is not
Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. Mohit is older than Kunal but younger than Sandeep.

⇒ Sandeep > Mohit > Kunal

II. Tarun is younger than Sandeep but older than Mohit.

⇒ Sandeep > Tarun > Mohit

Analysis:

Statement I alone → Not sufficient (Only gives relation among Sandeep, Mohit, Kunal; no info about Tarun and Rohan).

Statement II alone → Not sufficient (Only gives relation among Sandeep, Tarun, Mohit; no info about Kunal and Rohan).

Combining I and II:

⇒ Sandeep > Tarun > Mohit > Kunal

But, Rohan’s position is unknown, so oldest cannot be determined.

Here, both statements together are NOT sufficient.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

questions.question: Find the volume of largest possible sphere that can be inscribed in a cone whose base radius is 42√3 cm and slant height equal to the diameter of the base. (Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ For cone, inscribed sphere radius r = (R × h) / (R + l)

⇒ Given R = 42√3, l = 2R = 84√3

⇒ h = √(l² − R²) = √(3R²) = R√3 = 126

⇒ r = (42√3 × 126) / (42√3 + 84√3) = 42

⇒ Volume = (4/3)πr³ = (4/3) × (22/7) × 42³ = 310464

**∴ Answer = 310464 cm³**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base radius R = 42√3

Slant height l = diameter = 84√3

**Formula Used:**

h = √(l² − R²)

r = (R × h) / (R + l)

Volume = (4/3)πr³

**Calculation:**

⇒ h = √[(84√3)² − (42√3)²]

⇒ = √(21168 − 5292) = √15876 = 126

⇒ r = (42√3 × 126) / (42√3 + 84√3)

⇒ = (42 × 126) / 126 = 42

questions.question: When a spring is compressed from its equilibrium position, its potential energy will ___________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Elastic Potential Energy** is the energy stored as a result of applying a **force** to deform an elastic object. The energy is stored until the force is removed and the object springs back to its original shape, doing **work** in the process.
 
• In the case of a spring, the **potential energy** is given by the formula **U = 1/2 kx²**, where **k** is the **spring constant** (a measure of the stiffness of the spring) and **x** is the **displacement** from the **equilibrium position**.
 
• At the **equilibrium position**, the displacement **x** is **zero**, which means the **potential energy** is at its **minimum** (zero). *Hence, the statement that potential energy increases when moving away from equilibrium is correct.*
 
• When a spring is **compressed**, work is done **against** the **restoring force** of the spring. This work is stored in the form of **potential energy**. Since the displacement **x** is squared in the formula, whether the spring is **compressed** (negative x) or **stretched** (positive x), the value of **x²** is always **positive**, leading to an **increase** in energy. *Hence, the correct answer is that it will increase.*
 
• If the potential energy were to **decrease**, it would mean the spring is returning toward its **equilibrium** point from a deformed state. *Hence, the statement that potential energy decreases during compression is incorrect.*
 
• The **restoring force** exerted by the spring is proportional to the displacement but in the **opposite direction**, described by **Hooke’s Law** as **F = -kx**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hooke’s Law:** Proposed by **Robert Hooke** in **1676**, this law states that for relatively small deformations of an object, the **displacement** or size of the deformation is directly **proportional** to the deforming force or load.
 
• **Spring Constant (k):** The **SI unit** for the spring constant is **Newton per meter (N/m)**. A higher value of **k** indicates a **stiffer** spring that requires more force to compress or extend.
 
• **Conservation of Energy:** In an **ideal system** without **friction** or **air resistance**, the **mechanical energy** (the sum of **kinetic energy** and **potential energy**) remains **constant**. When a compressed spring is released, the **potential energy** is converted into **kinetic energy** as the spring moves back toward equilibrium.
 
• **Applications of Spring Energy:** This principle is utilized in various mechanical devices such as **clocks**, **shock absorbers** in vehicles, **trampolines**, and **recoil mechanisms** in firearms.
 
• **Work Done:** The **work done** to compress a spring by a distance **x** is equal to the area under the **Force-Displacement graph**, which forms a **triangle** with area **1/2 × base × height**, resulting in **1/2 × x × kx = 1/2 kx²**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Equilibrium Position:** This is the **natural length** of the spring where no external forces are acting on it, and it exerts no **restoring force**.
 
• **Conservative Force:** The force exerted by a spring is a **conservative force**, meaning the **work done** by or against the force depends only on the **initial and final positions** and not on the path taken.
 
• **Elastic Limit:** If a spring is compressed or stretched beyond its **elastic limit**, it will not return to its original shape and the **Hooke's Law** relation fails. This results in **permanent deformation** or **plasticity**.
 
• **Direction of Force:** During **compression**, the displacement is inward, but the **restoring force** acts **outward**. During **extension**, the displacement is outward, and the **restoring force** acts **inward**. In both cases, the **potential energy** increases as you move away from the **center**.

__
 
• The **Suez Canal** is an artificial sea-level waterway located in **Egypt**, which effectively connects the **Mediterranean Sea** to the **Red Sea** through the **Isthmus of Suez**. This makes the statement about it linking these two seas correct.
 
• It was officially opened on **November 17, 1869**, after a construction period of **10 years** led by the **Suez Canal Company**, founded by **Ferdinand de Lesseps**.
 
• The canal serves as a vital boundary separating **Africa** from **Asia** and provides the **shortest maritime route** between **Europe** and the lands surrounding the **Indian** and western **Pacific Oceans**.

• This is an **82 km (51 mile)** artificial waterway in **Panama** that connects the **Atlantic Ocean** with the **Pacific Ocean**.
 
• Opened in **1914**, it utilizes a sophisticated system of **locks** to lift ships **26 meters** above sea level to **Gatun Lake**.
 
• It is essential for trade between the East and West coasts of the **United States** and for routes connecting **Asia** with the **American East Coast**.
 
 
 
• **Strait of Malacca**:
 
 
• Located between the **Malay Peninsula** and the **Indonesian** island of **Sumatra**, it is the primary shipping channel between the **Indian Ocean** and the **Pacific Ocean**.
 
• It is a major maritime "chokepoint" through which about **25%** of the world's traded goods pass annually, linking major economies like **China, India, Japan,** and **South Korea**.
 
 
 
• **Bosporus Strait**:

• It is strategically significant for the transport of **oil** and **agricultural products** from the **Black Sea** region.

• **Ever Given Incident**: In **March 2021**, a massive container ship called the **Ever Given** ran aground in the canal due to high winds. questions.question: Which type of lens is used in a simple microscope?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biconvex**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **simple microscope** is an optical instrument used to obtain a magnified image of small objects. It essentially consists of a single **biconvex lens** with a short **focal length**.
 
• A **biconvex lens** (also known as a **convex lens** or **converging lens**) is thicker in the middle than at the edges. It works by converging light rays that pass through it to a specific point.
 
• The principle of a **simple microscope** is based on the fact that when an object is placed between the **optical center** and the **principal focus** of a **convex lens**, the image formed is **virtual**, **erect**, and **magnified**.
 
• The **magnifying power** of a simple microscope is defined by the formula **M = 1 + (D/f)**, where **D** is the **least distance of distinct vision** (standardized at **25 cm** for a normal human eye) and **f** is the **focal length** of the lens.
 
• These instruments are commonly used by **watchmakers**, **jewelers**, and **students** to observe tiny parts or organisms. Because it uses only one lens, the **magnification** is limited compared to a **compound microscope**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biconcave Lens:**

 
 
• A **biconcave lens** is a **diverging lens** that is thinner at the center than at the edges.
 
• It is primarily used in the correction of **Myopia** (nearsightedness), as it helps spread out light rays before they reach the eye.
 
• It always forms a **virtual**, **erect**, and **diminished** image, regardless of the object's position.
 
 
 
• **Cylindrical Lens:**
 
 
• A **cylindrical lens** focuses light into a line rather than a point.
 
• It is specifically used to correct **Astigmatism**, a vision condition caused by an irregular curvature of the cornea or lens.
 
• These lenses have different **refractive powers** in different planes.
 
 
 
• **Plano-concave Lens:**
 
 
• This lens has one flat (plano) surface and one inward-curving (concave) surface.
 
• It has a **negative focal length** and is used to expand light beams or increase focal lengths in **optical systems**.
 
 
 
• **History and Inventor:**
 
 
• The **simple microscope** was famously improved and used by **Antonie van Leeuwenhoek** in the **17th century**.
 
• Using high-quality **biconvex lenses**, he achieved magnifications of up to **275x**, allowing him to be the first to observe **bacteria** and **protozoa**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nature of Image:** In a simple microscope, the object must be very close to the lens (within its **focal length**). If the object is moved beyond the **focal point**, the image becomes **real** and **inverted**, which is not suitable for microscopic observation.
 
• **Power of Lens:** The **power (P)** of the lens is the reciprocal of its **focal length (f)** in meters, expressed in **Dioptres (D)**. A higher power lens provides greater **magnification**.
 
• **Least Distance of Distinct Vision (LDDV):** This is the minimum distance at which the **human eye** can see an object clearly without any strain. For a healthy adult, this value is **25 cm**.
 
• **Materials:** Modern lenses are typically made from high-quality **optical glass** or **plastics** like **polycarbonate** to ensure high **refractive index** and low **chromatic aberration**.

questions.question: Who is officially authorized to conduct environment audits under the Environment Audit Rules, 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Registered Environment Auditor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Environment Audit Rules, 2025**, formulated by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**, officially authorize a **Registered Environment Auditor** to conduct environmental audits for industrial and developmental projects.
 
• A **Registered Environment Auditor** is a professional or an entity that has undergone specific training and is formally registered with the **National Board for Quality Promotion (NBQP)** or the **Quality Council of India (QCI)** to ensure they meet the **competency standards** required for environmental assessment.
 
• The audit process is designed to evaluate the **environmental performance** of an organization, ensuring that its operations align with the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** and the **Air and Water Acts**.
 
• These auditors are responsible for verifying the **Environmental Statement** (commonly known as **Form V**), which industries must submit to the **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)** annually.
 
• The **Environment Audit Rules, 2025** aim to bring **transparency** and **accountability** to the environmental compliance mechanism by shifting from self-declaration to verified auditing by third-party **Registered Auditors**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scope of Environment Audit:**

 
 
• The audit encompasses **resource consumption** (water, electricity, raw materials), **waste generation** (solid, hazardous, and electronic waste), and **pollution control measures**.
 
• It identifies **gaps in compliance** and suggests **mitigation strategies** to reduce the **carbon footprint** of the industry.
 
• The **Environment Audit Rules, 2025** apply to **Category A and B** projects as defined under the **Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Ministry (MoEFCC):**
 
 
• The **MoEFCC** acts as the apex body for policy-making and implementation regarding **environmental protection** in **India**.
 
• The **year 2025** marks a significant shift towards **digital monitoring** and **real-time data** integration in environmental auditing through the **PARIVESH 2.0** portal.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility for Auditors:**
 
 
• To become a **Registered Environment Auditor**, an individual typically requires a **Post-Graduate Degree** in **Environmental Science**, **Chemistry**, or a **Bachelor's Degree** in **Engineering (Chemical/Environmental/Civil)**.
 
• Minimum **5 to 7 years** of **work experience** in environmental management or industrial pollution control is generally mandatory for registration.
 
• Candidates must pass a **National Level Examination** conducted by **designated agencies** to obtain their **certification** and **registration number**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distinction between Roles:**

 
 
• An **Environmental Consultant** may provide advice on **project planning** and **EIA reports**, but they do not possess the **statutory authority** to sign off on a formal **Environment Audit** unless they are also a **Registered Auditor**.
 
• A **Certified Environment Auditor** is a broader term, whereas **Registered Environment Auditor** is the specific **legal designation** used in the **2025 Rules**.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework:**
 
 
• **Section 3** and **Section 25** of the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** grant the **Central Government** the power to frame such rules for **environmental conservation**.
 
• Failure to conduct an audit by a **Registered Auditor** or submitting **fraudulent data** can lead to heavy **monetary penalties** or the **closure of industrial units**.
 
• The **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** often refers to these **audit reports** during judicial proceedings involving **environmental degradation** or **accidental pollution**.

⇒ Given difference = 53

⇒ P × 16/10000 = 53

⇒ P = 53 × 10000 / 16 = 33125

**∴ Answer = 33125**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Rate = 4%

Time = 2 years

CI = P[(1 + r/100)t − 1]

⇒ CI = P[(1.04)² − 1]

⇒ Difference = CI − SI

⇒ = 0.0816P − 0.08P = 0.0016P

⇒ 0.0016P = 53

⇒ P = 53 / 0.0016 = 33125

**∴ The correct answer is ₹33125.**

Right triangle ABC, ∠B = 90°

tan A = opposite/adjacent

⇒ tan A = BC/AB = 5/12

⇒ cot C = BC/AB = 5/12

questions.question: Oriya’ was replaced with ‘Odia’ in the Eighth Schedule by which Constitutional Amendment?

The correct answer is __**96th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **96th Constitutional Amendment Act** was passed by the **Parliament of India** in the year **2011**.
 
• This amendment specifically aimed to substitute the spelling of the language listed in the **Eighth Schedule** from **‘Oriya’** to **‘Odia’**. ***Hence, the 96th Amendment is the correct option.***
 
• The **Eighth Schedule** of the **Constitution of India** consists of a list of **22 official languages** recognized by the state, and **Odia** is one of the prominent classical languages included in this list.
 
• The change in the name of the language was a follow-up to the **Orissa (Alteration of Name) Act, 2011**, which changed the name of the state from **Orissa** to **Odisha**.
 
• This modification was sought to reflect the correct **phonetic** and **linguistic** pronunciation of the language as used by the native speakers in the state of **Odisha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **97th Amendment Act, 2011**:

 
 
• This amendment provided **constitutional status** and protection to **co-operative societies** in India.
 
• It inserted **Article 43B** in the **Directive Principles of State Policy** and added **Part IXB** to the Constitution.
 
• It also made the right to form **co-operative societies** a **Fundamental Right** under **Article 19(1)(c)**. ***Hence, this statement is not related to the renaming of the language.***
 
 
 
• **95th Amendment Act, 2009**:
 
 
• It extended the **reservation** of seats for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in the **Lok Sabha** and the **State Legislative Assemblies**.
 
• The period of reservation was extended from **60 years** to **70 years** (until **January 25, 2020**).
 
• It also extended the representation of the **Anglo-Indian community** by nomination. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect in the context of the question.***
 
 
 
• **94th Amendment Act, 2006**:
 
 
• This amendment concerned the appointment of a **Minister of Tribal Welfare** in certain states.
 
• It exempted **Bihar** from the obligation to have a tribal welfare minister while extending this provision to the newly created states of **Jharkhand** and **Chhattisgarh** under **Article 164(1)**. ***Hence, this statement is not the correct answer.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of the Eighth Schedule**: Originally, the **Eighth Schedule** contained **14 languages**. Over the years, through various **Constitutional Amendments**, the number has increased to **22**.
 
• **Significant Language Amendments**:
 
 
• **21st Amendment Act, 1967**: Added **Sindhi** as the **15th language**.
 
• **71st Amendment Act, 1992**: Added **Konkani**, **Manipuri**, and **Nepali**.
 
• **92nd Amendment Act, 2003**: Added **Bodo**, **Dogri**, **Maithili**, and **Santhali**.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions**: **Article 344(1)** and **Article 351** of the **Indian Constitution** are the primary articles that deal with the **Eighth Schedule** and the development of the **Hindi language** and other regional languages.
 
• **Odia as a Classical Language**: In **February 2014**, **Odia** was declared the **sixth classical language** of India by the **Union Cabinet**, joining the ranks of **Tamil**, **Sanskrit**, **Telugu**, **Kannada**, and **Malayalam**.

questions.question: How many nations became signatories to the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime in December 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__72__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Based on the United Nations Treaty Collection, one nation, Fiji, became a signatory to the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime in December 2025.
 
• While the treaty officially opened for signature at a high-level ceremony in Hanoi, Vietnam, on 25–26 October 2025, where 72 participants (71 states and the European Union) signed, the process remains open at the UN Headquarters in New York until 31 December 2026.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Comparison with the Budapest Convention:** Before the UN treaty, the **Council of Europe’s Budapest Convention (2001)** was the primary international treaty on cybercrime, but it was not globally universal as many **developing nations** and countries like **Russia** and **China** were not parties to it.
 
• **Role of UNODC:** The **United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)** serves as the **secretariat** for the convention, providing **technical assistance** and **capacity-building** support to member states to implement the treaty's provisions effectively.
 
• **Scope of Digital Crimes:** The convention covers a wide range of crimes, including **financial fraud**, **identity theft**, **cyber-terrorism**, and **online grooming**, ensuring that perpetrators cannot find **safe havens** in countries with weak digital laws.
 
• **Human Rights Safeguards:** During the drafting phase, several **civil society organizations** and **tech companies** expressed concerns regarding **state surveillance**; hence, the final text includes provisions to balance **security needs** with **fundamental human rights** and **privacy**.
 
• **Global Inclusion:** Unlike previous regional agreements, this **United Nations** led initiative ensures that **low-income** and **developing nations** receive the necessary **technological resources** and **training** to protect their **critical infrastructure**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ratification Process:** Becoming a **signatory** is the first step; however, the convention only comes into **force** once a specific number of nations (usually **30 to 40** depending on the treaty clause) complete the **ratification** process in their respective **national parliaments**.
 
• **Electronic Evidence:** One of the most vital features of the **2025** agreement is the streamlined process for **cross-border data requests**, allowing law enforcement agencies to obtain **digital evidence** from service providers located in other **signatory nations**.
 
• **Signatory vs. Accession:** While **151** nations signed the treaty during the initial window in **2025**, other countries can join later through a process called **accession**, which carries the same **legal obligations**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The push for this treaty was notably led by **Russia** and supported by a diverse group of nations, reflecting a shift toward a **multipolar** approach to **internet governance** and **cybersecurity**.

questions.question: Which of the following locations stores recently opened files in Windows for quick access?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quick Access**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Quick Access** is a feature introduced in **Windows 10** that serves as a personalized navigation hub within **File Explorer**. It replaces the "Favorites" functionality found in older versions like **Windows 7** and **Windows 8**.
 
• The primary **function** of **Quick Access** is to automatically track and display a list of **recently opened files** and **frequently used folders**, allowing users to resume their work quickly without digging through deep directory structures. ***Hence, this option is correct.***
 
• By **default**, when a user opens a new **File Explorer** window, it lands on the **Quick Access** view. This view typically shows the **10 most frequent folders** and the **20 most recent files**.
 
• It offers a **customization feature** where users can "Pin" specific folders to the **Quick Access** section in the **Navigation Pane**. This ensures that essential project folders remain permanently accessible regardless of how many other files are opened.
 
• The **location** of the **Quick Access** icon is usually at the very top of the left-hand **Navigation Pane** in any folder window, marked with a **blue star icon**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Recycle Bin**:

 
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is a system folder where **deleted files** are temporarily stored before they are permanently removed from the **hard drive**.
 
• Its **use** is to provide a safety net for accidental deletions, but it does not track or store shortcuts to recently opened active files. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Desktop**:
 
 
• The **Desktop** is the primary **user interface** and workspace seen immediately after logging into **Windows**.
 
• While users can manually place shortcuts or files on the **Desktop** for easy reach, it does not function as an automated log of recently accessed documents from across the system. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Control Panel**:
 
 
• The **Control Panel** is a centralized **utility** used to manage **system settings**, hardware configurations, and software installations.
 
• It contains applets for **User Accounts**, **Network and Sharing Center**, and **Device Manager**, but it is not intended for file navigation or viewing document history. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **File Explorer**:
 
 
• Formerly known as **Windows Explorer**, this **application** is the file management system for the **Windows Operating System**. It allows users to browse **local disks**, **cloud storage** like **OneDrive**, and network locations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Privacy and Management**: Users can manage what appears in **Quick Access** through **Folder Options** (or **File Explorer Options**). Under the **Privacy** section of the **General** tab, users can click **Clear** to wipe the history of **File Explorer**.
 
• **Data Handling**: Disabling the "Show recently used files in Quick access" checkbox prevents **Windows** from recording recent file history in this specific location, which is a common **privacy feature** for shared computers.
